steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Voila, this is our reconstructed ward!

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: It's exactly the same as before, isn't it? Eve, have you seen what the clinic looked like before?

steps.speaker: Eve
steps.content: No. Ever since I lost my legs, I've hardly gone out.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: I see... It's okay, now you've seen it!

steps.speaker: Francisco
steps.content: Hey, is this our new friend?
A burly man greets the nurse with a warm smile.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Hehe, Eve is a guest the MBCC has temporarily entrusted to us!

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Now, let me introduce you. This is Francisco the great painter!

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: How are you recovering?

steps.speaker: Francisco
steps.content: Thanks to you, it's going great! Recreating those Eastside artists' masterpieces is just a piece of cake!

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Alright, alright, show off your talent once you're discharged.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Don't waste it in my notebook!
The nurse tears a page from her notebook and gives it back to Francisco. Eve sees that the drawing on it is just some crooked stick figures.

steps.speaker: Francisco
steps.content: Miss Eve is looking at my drawing? Would you like me to do a portrait for you?

steps.speaker: Eve
steps.content: Um... Thank you?
Eve gives a noncommittal answer while eyeing Francisco's drawing.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: I still have to introduce Eve to the others here. You're interrupting us.
Francisco laughs unconcernedly and watches the nurse push Eve away.

steps.speaker: Rhona
steps.content: I wrote a new brain teaser! Come and have a guess!

steps.speaker: Rhona
steps.content: What can be produced in the North, East, South, and West of DisCity?
The lively scene not far away attracts the nurse and Eve's attention again. A little girl is standing on a bed, announcing loudly.

steps.speaker: Patients
steps.content: What is it, what is it?

steps.speaker: Rhona
steps.content: Hehe, it's... melon!
The crowd bursts into laughter over the joke Eve can't understand.

steps.speaker: Patients
steps.content: Hahaha! Rhona, you should come and do a stand-up comedy at my diner one day. People will love it!

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Wow, count me in!
The nurse joins the boisterous crowd.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: You must think the joke is lame, right?

steps.speaker: Eve
steps.content: Am I a killjoy here?
The nurse smiles and continues to make the introduction enthusiastically.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Look over there, that's Andrew. He used to be the owner of a diner before he was admitted to the clinic!

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: That's Albert. I heard he used to be a famous big eater in Syndicate. People keep saying he should go to Eastside and start a livestreaming career. He'd definitely make a name for himself!

Eve looks at the people the nurse is introducing to her. One is in ragged patched-up clothes, and the other is skinny as a skeleton. But strangely, as they bicker with one another, their demeanor seems to still fit the nurse's descriptions.

steps.speaker: Albert
steps.content: Hahaha, if Rhona's doing a stand-up performance, I definitely have to be there! And I'll empty every last bit of food in Andrew's restaurant!

steps.speaker: Andrew
steps.content: Keep talking. As if you can keep up with my cooking speed!
Horsing around boisterously, they don't appear like patients at all.
Eve leans in close to the nurse and whispers.

steps.speaker: Eve
steps.content: What brought them to the clinic?

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: The folks in Syndicate have a rough life. They don't go to the doctor for minor ailments or injuries.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: The only thing that can bring them here... is Mania.
The nurse's expression darkens for a moment, but she quickly regains her smile.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Alright, alright, that's enough bluffing for now! Everyone line up.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Time for a blood test!
Like students in a classroom, the lively group obediently return to their respective spaces and quiet down.
As the other nurses start to run tests on them one by one, the nurse pushes Eve to a quiet corridor.

steps.speaker: Helmet Girl
steps.content: Sigh, those guys can't sit still for a minute.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: I was going to show you around this place, but it turned out a bit chaotic.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: I hope that didn't bother you too much?
Eve is indeed not used to being surrounded by so many people, but strangely, she doesn't feel repulsed.

steps.speaker: Eve
steps.content: No, it's fine. I'm glad they seem cheerful...

steps.speaker: Eve
steps.content: It feels... familiar...

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Hehe, did you have boastful friends like that too?
Several figures emerge in her mind, and Eve can't help but smile.

steps.speaker: Eve
steps.content: I wouldn't call them boastful. They simply liked to talk about that beautiful world they imagined...

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Hmm, even if they knew it might never come true, right?
Her inner thoughts are seen through by someone she just met. Eve widens her eyes uncharacteristically.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Of course Chief has told us all about you before entrusting you to us.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: You've heard a lot of little lies like that, haven't you?

steps.speaker: Eve
steps.content: I truly don't understand... You know Mr. Francisco would never become a great painter. Why are you still telling him those things?

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Well, I didn't understand it at first either!

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: But when my arm was corrupted, the nurse who took care of me told me that I would be cured and could live a normal life.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: And just like magic, the wound somehow hurt less...
The nurse touches her arm a little bashfully.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Truth be told, it was never possible. After all, I had an entire arm removed. I knew she was just comforting me.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: But sometimes, a lie might just be the most effective painkiller. At least it made me feel better at that time.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: That's why I'm giving a dose to everyone now! I've gotten used to it over time...
The alarm suddenly goes off in the corridor, an urgent red light signaling unknown danger.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Oh, excuse me, I kept talking about my personal story. I think they need me for an important task. Tell me your story next time, Eve!
The nurse parks Eve's wheelchair in a safe corner and hurries away.

steps.speaker: Eve
steps.content: Friendly, a little careless, and always in a rush. Is everyone here like this?
Alone in that corner, Eve begins observing her surroundings.
Unlike the factory, the hospital's corridor has many windows through which one can see the sky.
A flock of startled birds fly by, seeming to be coming from the direction of the Syndican slum.

steps.speaker: Eve
steps.content: ...I wonder what that rag doll in gray clothes is doing now?
Doll? Do you have a doll too?
She suddenly hears a childish voice behind her.
Eve turns the wheelchair around slowly and sees a little girl holding a ragged doll.
The IV line has left marks on the little girl's hand.

steps.speaker: Lily
steps.content: I'm Lily. Are you also a patient here? I've never seen you!

steps.speaker: Eve
steps.content: Hi Lily, I'm Eve. I'm just here temporarily.

steps.speaker: Lily
steps.content: I see. So you don't have Mania?

steps.speaker: Eve
steps.content: I... I'm already a Sinner.

steps.speaker: Lily
steps.content: A Sinner?! How cool!
Lily excitedly raises the doll in her hand.

steps.speaker: Lily
steps.content: Could you maybe fix my doll with your power?
That thing can hardly be called a doll. It's just a few rags sewn together and stuffed with cotton. Eve can't make out the original shape, but she can feel the traces of corruption.
Eve leans in and unintentionally sees the tag on Lily's hand.
Patient Name: Lily
Mania Contamination Level: High
<i>Contamination Removal Surgery Date: Scheduled within this week<i>

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: But sometimes, a lie might just be the most effective painkiller. At least it made me feel better at that time.
I'm going to turn those lies into truths and use the power accumulated from the tomorrows to create a better world for you, and for everyone.

steps.speaker: Lily
steps.content: Eve? Why are you so quiet... It can't be fixed, can it?

steps.speaker: Eve
steps.content: Yes, it can, give it to me. Soon it'll look as good as new.

steps.speaker: Andrew
steps.content: So, Rhona...
The nurse turns her back and wipes away her tears, shaking her head.

steps.speaker: Albert
steps.content: I see... She's going to tell jokes to everyone in heaven...

steps.speaker: Francisco
steps.content: Then I'll draw a portrait for her. I'm sure Rhona will like it.
